parts.description: A single piece of popped popcorn with an irregular, fluffy white shape and slightly browned inner crevices.
parts.reasoning: The object is a piece of popcorn, which is essentially expanded starch. It is characterized by extremely low density and low mass. A typical piece weighs a fraction of a gram (estimated here at 0.3 grams). Its highly porous and airy structure results in a very low restitution (bounciness), as it tends to absorb impacts rather than rebound. The dry, irregular surface provides moderate friction. For simulation in Isaac Sim, the highly irregular shape with multiple protruding lobes and concavities necessitates 'convex_decomposition' for accurate collision geometry, allowing pieces to realistically settle and interlock. Because of its very low mass and small size, Continuous Collision Detection (CCD) is highly recommended to prevent tunneling when subjected to forces or when falling.
